title: Mobile blood gas analysis "mobOx"
summary:
Rapid determination of laboratory values is an indispensable part of acute care for critically ill patients in acute and emergency medicine. As much information about the patient as possible must be obtained in the shortest possible time. Unfortunately, with the exception of measuring blood sugar, routine measurement of laboratory values at the scene of an emergency has not yet become established in pre-hospital emergency medicine. Real point-of-care (POC) measurements are also only occasionally carried out in the operating room. One possible reason for this may be the unsuitability of the devices available on the market. Some of these are quite large (about the size of a shoe box) and susceptible to extreme temperatures. In addition, the test cuvettes have a limited shelf life and sometimes have to be specially stored. 
We are convinced that the project described here is suitable for overcoming many of the disadvantages of the devices available to date and will therefore not only increase the acceptance of measuring laboratory values at the point of use, but could possibly also make this procedure the standard in the operating theater. The handiness of the device to be tested in conjunction with the new measurement technology form the necessary basis for this. In order to test the usability of the test device, patients undergoing major surgery, during which blood gas analyses are carried out regularly anyway, are to be measured with the test device using the residual blood volume that would otherwise be discarded. A copy of the results measured with the gold standard is then compared (offline) with the results of the test device. The results of the test device are not made available to the treating physicians, so there is no risk of the test device influencing the patient's therapy. Through this study, we collect valuable results that serve to optimize the algorithm and assess the usability of the test device. There is no additional risk for the patients participating in the study. The only difference is that a larger amount of residual blood is discarded if patients do not participate than if they do.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Presence of broad consent (UKSH, Lübeck) or a signed declaration of consent (BG Klinikum Hamburg) and the installation of an arterial catheter for intraoperative blood sampling, which is necessary for the planned procedure anyway.
Exclusion criteria:
Thalassemia, hemochromatosis, simultaneous therapy with methylene blue and indigocarmine, incapacity to consent.
